thread:
alexa: getting pages for runtime latencies + a bunch of kv-cache errors. looks like something noisy in log ingest is firing our log-based alerts, paging oncall repeatedly :grimacing:
incident-bot: Incident #2453 created — high error rate on /v2/generate (hosted), paging eng-sre and eng-runtime
Ben S: oncall-1 here, I'm looking — can we mute the log alert for kv-cache errors while we triage? it's spamming PD
Maya R: +1. I think it's the 'Timeout while reading KV shard' transient we saw last week. we should narrow query rather than full mute if possible
Chris P: quick customer impact note: Dedicated customers in us-west saw ~3–6% 5xx increase for ~7m. no data exfil. tickets incoming from three customers (CS notified)
Ben S: ok I'm going to silence the noisy log-based rule for 30m and create a temporary suppression in PD. will add to thread after I do
pagerduty-bot: Alert suppression created by Ben S — 30 minutes for rule: logs/redwood-kv-cache-errors
Ben S: suppressed. now dumping a couple of representative log lines to see pattern:
```
ERROR kv/shard.go:247: Timeout while reading KV shard id=shard-12 node=ip-10-4-5-21 tx=0x7f3a
WARN kv/cache.go:102: cache miss for key=user-... src=replica
ERROR kv/shard.go:247: Timeout while reading KV shard id=shard-7 node=ip-10-4-2-18 tx=0x5c1b
ERROR kv/shard.go:312: Permanent shard failure id=shard-7 reason=OOM
```
Maya R: pattern: most are transient timeouts, but the 'Permanent shard failure' should still alert. current log rule is basically `status:ERROR AND message:/kv shard/` which is too broad
Chris P: suggest changing the query to exclude transient timeouts and only match when we see either `Permanent` or repeated timeouts per host in a short window
alexa: can we do that purely in the log query? or do we need a metric-based rule for repeats?
Maya R: we can tighten the query first: use a regex that matches `Permanent` or `Timeout.*(?!while reading KV shard)` — actually better to explicitly match Permanent or Timeout with more context. proposed query (StackQuery syntax):
```
(status:ERROR) AND (message:/Permanent shard failure/ OR message:/Timeout while reading KV shard.*tx=/)
```
That way we still catch the permanent failures and the timeouts that include transaction id (which correlate with real errors) and ignore other noisy WARN-level cache misses
Ben S: I updated the alert rule in Logging -> Alerts. New rule expression: `status:ERROR AND (message:/Permanent shard failure/ OR message:/Timeout while reading KV shard.*tx=[0-9a-f]+)/`
triage-bot: Rule updated by Ben S — logs/redwood-kv-cache-errors. Old threshold preserved.
Chris P: also added a regex signature to ignore known benign `cache miss` lines: message:/cache miss for key=.*/ with severity:info
alexa: good. let's also add a note in the runbook to escalate if the modified rule fires >5 hosts in 5m (to catch broad regressions)
Maya R: created saved search `kv-failures-signature` and a dashboard panel that shows `count by host where message matches (Permanent|Timeout.*tx=`)
Maya R: linking query and dashboard in the ticket: https://grafana.company/redwood/d/kvcache/kv-failures
Ben S: re-enabled alerts (with new query) and removed suppression — monitoring for the next 20m
incident-bot: Incident #2453 status changed to "mitigated" by Ben S
Chris P: customer impact summary posted to CS: Dedicated customers saw transient latency spikes and small % 5xx increase. root cause: transient KV timeouts during a noisy GC on a subset of hosts. fix: tuned alerting rules to reduce noise, added dashboard, new runbook entry. follow-ups: infra to investigate GC schedule for shards (owner: Maya R), runtime team to add circuit-breaker in client (owner: Chris P)

- Maya R: create metric-based burst detector and link to PD (due 2026-03-22)
- Chris P: implement client-side circuit-breaker and retry throttling (due 2026-04-02)

Maya R: recorded the updated logging rule and query in the alerts doc: https://docs.internal/redwood/alerts#kv-cache-errors and added sample logs + regex examples
alexa: thanks team. if we see any reoccurrence let's escalate immediately. closing this thread — I'll kick off the postmortem doc template later and assign reviewers
